title: Data Access and Open Finance
summary: How open banking and open finance frameworks enable customer-permissioned data sharing, the design choices behind them, and the competition, privacy and security trade-offs supervisors need to understand.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How open banking and open finance frameworks enable customer-permissioned data sharing, the design choices behind them, and the competition, privacy and security trade-offs supervisors need to understand.
Learning Objectives: Explain the design of open banking and open finance frameworks
Assess consent, liability and security arrangements for data sharing
Evaluate the risk that data access entrenches rather than reduces platform power
Syllabus: Open banking to open finance: scope and data categories
APIs, standards, consent dashboards and liability models
Data protection, fraud and cybersecurity risks in data sharing
Reciprocity and data flows between big tech and incumbents
Intended Audience: Supervisors of banks, payment and e-money institutions, lenders and insurers that partner with platforms or distribute through them
Policy, innovation and authorisation staff dealing with new entrants, perimeter questions and open finance
Senior managers coordinating with competition, data protection and consumer authorities
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of banking, payments or conduct supervision is helpful. No technical background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
FSB, Enhancing Cross-border Payments: Stage 3 Roadmap (2020)
